title: I Invoked UCC 1-308 in Court, Here's What Happened
summary: Acted courtroom scenario showing how to use a UCC 1-308 reservation-of-rights affidavit to challenge jurisdiction over a traffic ticket, with templates sold via Patreon.

assertions.quote: without waving any of my rights as preserved in my reservation of rights under UCC 1-3 8

verdicts.note: UCC 1-308 applies to commercial contracts; courts hold it gives no defence to criminal or traffic charges.
The defendant reserved rights 'per UCC 1-308 without prejudice' and withheld consent, yet was convicted; the court notes UCC arguments are unavailing.

UCC 1-308's text and official comment: it lets a party keep performing a commercial contract under protest during a dispute without waiving reserved rights. It says nothing about courts or criminal law.

assertions.quote: I respectfully challenge the jurisdiction of this court to enforce a contract to which I have not consented
the ticket presented constitutes an offer to contract which I did not agree to

verdicts.note: A citation is a charging document under statute, not a contract offer; refusing it does not stop prosecution.
In Ohio the uniform traffic ticket serves as the complaint and summons, a charging document rather than an offer to contract.

assertions.quote: without such evidence I move for this case to be dismissed

verdicts.note: Courts deny such motions as frivolous; dismissals that occur come from ordinary grounds like a missing officer.
The defendant's notice to abate, sovereignty affidavit and jurisdiction challenge were summarily overruled and he was convicted on all traffic and related charges; one case.
